name: cinatra
workload: wrk -t4 -c240 -d35s against GET /plaintext, identical response body/headers, comparing cinatra, drogon, brpc and a bare nginx config on the same host
claimed_speedup: cinatra 247841 req/s vs nginx 239629 req/s (~3% faster); also beat drogon (216982 req/s) and brpc (147954 req/s) in the same run (verbatim numbers from repo doc)
hardware: 4-core, 2.3GHz Ubuntu cloud VM (exact CPU model not stated)
tradeoffs: Header-only, requires C++20 coroutines (needs a recent GCC/Clang, via async_simple); nginx side of the comparison was a bare static-response config, not a full reverse-proxy workload
caveats: Margin over nginx is small (~3%); CPU model not specified, only core count/clock given; numbers come from the project's own benchmark, not independently reproduced; benchmark and nginx config are both included in the same doc (section 8) so it is reproducible in principle
found_via: TechEmpower framework benchmarks winners plaintext json -> TechEmpower C++ frameworks list (frameworks/C++/cinatra) -> cinatra's own repo doc lang/coroutine_based_http_lib.md

name: Pingora
workload: Cloudflare production edge traffic, comparing the retired NGINX-based proxy service to Pingora at scale (real production load, not a synthetic benchmark)
claimed_speedup: 5ms lower median TTFB, 80ms lower p95 TTFB, ~70% less CPU and ~67% less memory at equivalent traffic; one customer's connection reuse ratio rose from 87.1% to 99.92% (160x fewer new origin connections) (verbatim from blog)
stars_or_usage: 27.5k stars; runs Cloudflare's production edge proxy
tradeoffs: Pingora is a proxy-building framework/library, not a drop-in nginx replacement or config-compatible server; the blog attributes gains to architecture (shared connection pools, multithreading vs. multiprocessing) rather than raw per-request speed
caveats: No controlled or reproducible benchmark; aggregate production metrics with no stated hardware or measurement methodology; the blog explicitly says the improvement is 'not because we run code faster'
found_via: http-servers-frameworks faster than nginx blog shootout -> Cloudflare engineering blog post on Pingora

name: http.zig (httpz)

claimed_speedup: 171397.6 req/s vs actix-web 163414.7 req/s at concurrency 512 (~5% faster; derived from page data)
hardware: benchmark metadata reports 16 vCPUs, cpu_name 'M1 Eight-Core Processor', machine 'x86_64' (self-contradictory, see caveats)
